Your house has a lot of important information. Do you know where to find it?

Appliance model numbers, warranty documents, repair history, and service contacts are easy to forget about until something stops working. Having those details organized can make an unexpected problem easier to handle.

I created The Home Systems Record to help homeowners keep that information together: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

The repair itself isn't always the first headache when something breaks at home.

You may need to track down the appliance model number, check whether a warranty is still active, or remember which company handled the last service call. That search can be frustrating when the information is scattered.

Try picking one appliance today and recording its model number, warranty details, and service contact. Keep the information somewhere everyone in your household can find it.

You don't need to document every detail of your house to create a useful home reference.

Start with four things: equipment models and filter sizes, warranty dates and documents, shutoff locations and service contacts, and repair history. Those basics can help when maintenance or repairs come up.

The Home Systems Record includes 12 printable worksheets to organize important household details: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

A home reference system doesn't need to be complicated to be useful.

Instead of keeping manuals in one drawer, warranty information in an email inbox, and service contacts on random receipts, give those details one consistent place to live. A binder or organized digital folder can work.

Try creating a dedicated home information folder this week. Start with your HVAC system, water heater, and major appliances, then add records as you find them.

When something breaks at home, knowing where to start can make a difference.

Having equipment details, service history, and important contacts ready won't fix the problem for you. But it can reduce the time spent searching for paperwork while you're trying to arrange the next step.

The Home Systems Record is a printable reference kit designed for exactly this kind of preparation: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

A little home organization can save a lot of unnecessary searching later.

Model numbers, filter sizes, warranty details, shutoff locations, and repair records are all worth keeping somewhere accessible. The goal isn't to create more paperwork. It's to make the information you already have easier to use.

If you were putting together a home reference binder, what's the first piece of information you'd want to include?
